stem: A discrete random variable X has the following probability distribution: P(X=0) = 0.1, P(X=1) = 0.3, P(X=2) = k, P(X=3) = 0.2. What is the value of k?

per_option_rationale.rationale: All probabilities must sum to 1: 0.1 + 0.3 + k + 0.2 = 1 => k = 1 - 0.6 = 0.4.
0.3 arises from summing only P(X=0) and P(X=3) as 0.1+0.2=0.3 and setting k=0.3, misreading the constraint.
0.6 arises from computing the sum of the known probabilities (0.1+0.3+0.2=0.6) but then setting k=0.6 rather than k=1-0.6=0.4.
0.2 is the value of P(X=3), not k; the student misreads which probability is the unknown.

explanation: A valid probability distribution must satisfy the axiom that all probabilities sum to 1. Solving: 0.1 + 0.3 + k + 0.2 = 1 gives k = 0.4.

explanation_sections.punchline: Sum of all PMF values = 1 is the defining constraint for any valid probability distribution.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify model: discrete random variable PMF completeness. Apply sum rule: sum of all P(X=x) = 1. Substitute known values: 0.1 + 0.3 + k + 0.2 = 1. Solve: k = 1 - 0.6 = 0.4.
explanation_sections.lesson: Every probability distribution must sum to exactly 1; use this to find any missing probability.
explanation_sections.timing: 25 seconds. Sum the known values (0.6), subtract from 1. Trap: using the sum (0.6) as the answer instead of 1 - 0.6.
